# awscc_quicksight_assignment (Resource)

Resource Type definition for AWS::QuickSight::Assignment, which manages an Amazon QuickSight IAM policy assignment that attaches an IAM policy to specified QuickSight users or groups within a namespace.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `assignment_name` (String) The name of the assignment, also called a rule. The name must be unique within the AWS account.
- `assignment_status` (String) The status of the assignment.
- `namespace` (String) The namespace that contains the assignment.

### Optional

- `identities` (Map of List of String) The QuickSight users, groups, or both that you want to assign the policy to. This maps identity type to a list of identity names.
- `policy_arn` (String) The ARN for the IAM policy to apply to the QuickSight users and groups specified in this assignment.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM policy assignment. This is a synthesized identifier composed of the namespace and assignment name.
- `assignment_id` (String) The ID for the IAM policy assignment.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_quicksight_assignment.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM policy assignment

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_quicksight_assignment.example
  id = "arn"

```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:
